newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police to use cobras to combat riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police to use cobras to combat riots.

text.p: Indonesian police on the outskirts of the capital Jakarta plan to use poisonous cobras against "brutal rioters", a senior officer said on Thursday.

Lieutenant-Colonel Alex Riatmodjo, head of of the Bekasi police district and a graduate of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Academy in the United States, said the poisonious cobras were being examined as a crowd control method.
"Now we have three weapons -- the cobra, the dog and hot silver (bullets)," Riatmodjo told Reuters.

Seven snakes were already in a basket and glass container at the Bekasi police station, 40 km (25 miles) east of the city centre, he said. The precinct planned to acquire a total of 24 cobras, including some king cobras, for its trials, he added.

"If police face brutal rioters we have an officer who is able to control the cobras. Holding it in his hand, he would face the rioters, to lower their spirit," he said, when asked how he thought the technique would work.

Riatmodjo said Bekasi police have not yet tried the method, adding the snakes did not normally attack people unless they were disturbed so police would have to stir up the reptiles themselves before they were used against rioters.
